d: Explains how to customize the global lighting with the Lighting service.
h:
The Lighting service contains properties that you can adjust to update and customize the global lighting in a game. There are five categories of lighting properties:

  • Color — Configures hue within the game.
  • Intensity — Configures the intensity or amount of light hitting the camera.
  • Shadows — Configures how a user experiences shadows within the game.
  • Appearance — Properties that determine the lighting style and lighting/shading quality or view distance prioritization.
  • Environment — Configures the conditions of the game's world, such as the time of day and geographic latitude.

Color

Ambient

The Ambient property sets a hue for the entirety of a game. This property affects the lighting for both outdoor and indoor environments.

OutdoorAmbient

The OutdoorAmbient property sets a hue for outdoor areas of a game. This can help simulate how the ambient color of real-life lighting changes throughout the day. For example, sunlight in the early morning or late afternoon is usually warmer and more pink and orange in tone, while late evening is usually cooler and more blue and purple in tone.

In the following images, note that the lighting inside the garage and cafe doesn't change like it would if you were changing the Ambient property.

ColorShift_Top

The ColorShift_Top property sets a hue that reflects from surfaces facing the sun or moon.

ColorShift_Bottom

The ColorShift_Bottom property sets a hue that reflects from surfaces that are facing away from the sun or moon.

In the following images, note the hue change on the sandstone wall facing away from the sun.

Intensity

Brightness

The Brightness property sets the intensity of illumination. This can help increase the contrast between brightly illuminated areas and shadows, simulating bright sunshine and warmer weather.

ExposureCompensation

The ExposureCompensation property applies exposure to a game. Exposure is the amount of light that reaches the camera.

A lower value is similar to under-exposure in photography, while a higher value is similar to over-exposure.

Shadows

GlobalShadows

When enabled, the GlobalShadows property renders shadows.

ShadowSoftness

The ShadowSoftness property adjusts how blurry shadows are from a value of 0 (hard edges) to 1 (soft edges). This property is only valid when LightingStyle is set to Realistic.

Appearance

LightingStyle

LightingStyle indicates the artistic intent behind lighting in the game, as an LightingStyle option. Realistic provides the most advanced and realistic lighting and shadows Roblox can deliver, while Soft produces a flat, retro‑Roblox look with softer lights and shadows.

PrioritizeLightingQuality

The PrioritizeLightingQuality property indicates whether you prefer lighting/shading quality or view distance to scale down first. As the rendering quality level reduces, a setting of true prioritizes features such as advanced shadows and high‑quality shaders at closer distances, while a setting of false prioritizes view distance. If lighting and shadows are very important to the artistic feel of your game, set this to true.

Environment

ClockTime and TimeOfDay

The ClockTime and TimeOfDay property both represent the current time of day in hours, and they are directly related; if you change one property, the other also changes.

The only difference between these properties is their numeric value; ClockTime represents time from hour 0 through 24 while TimeOfDay represents time through a 24 hour string.

Note that each property doesn't follow the actual time of day, and they will not change during a game unless changed through a script.

GeographicLatitude

The GeographicLatitude property represents the geographic latitude in degrees. Note that while this property changes the position of the sun and moon, it does not change the ClockTime and TimeOfDay properties.

EnvironmentDiffuseScale

The EnvironmentDiffuseScale property determines how much ambient light is derived from the environment.

In the following images, note how the ambient light changes, particularly inside the kitchen of the ramen shop.

EnvironmentSpecularScale

The EnvironmentSpecularScale property determines how much specular light is derived from the environment. When set near a value of 1, smooth objects better reflect the environment and metal appears more realistic.

kid.simple: The `Lighting` service has settings that control the light for your whole game world. You can tint everything a color, make the sun brighter, turn shadows on or off, choose a realistic or soft style, and set the time of day. These settings change the whole mood of your game, from a sunny beach to a spooky night. You can change them in the Properties window or with a script.
kid.analogy: The Lighting service is like the master light switchboard in a theater. One panel controls the color of the stage lights, how bright they are, how sharp the shadows look, and whether it looks like morning or night.
keyPoints: Lighting properties fall into five groups: color, intensity, shadows, appearance, and environment.
`Ambient` tints the whole game, indoors and outdoors. `OutdoorAmbient` tints only outdoor areas.
`ColorShift_Top` tints surfaces facing the sun or moon; `ColorShift_Bottom` tints surfaces facing away.
`Brightness` sets how strong the light is, and `ExposureCompensation` makes the whole picture darker (negative) or brighter (positive), like a camera setting.
`GlobalShadows` turns shadows on or off. `ShadowSoftness` goes from 0 (sharp edges) to 1 (blurry edges) and only works with the Realistic style.
`LightingStyle` can be `Realistic` for advanced lighting or `Soft` for a flatter, classic Roblox look.
`ClockTime` (a number from 0 to 24) and `TimeOfDay` (text like "17:00:00") both set the time. Changing one changes the other.
Time does not move by itself. To make a day-night cycle, change `ClockTime` with a script.

terms.global lighting: Lighting settings that affect the entire world at once.
terms.hue / tint: A color added on top of everything, like looking through orange sunglasses.
terms.Ambient: The base light color everywhere, even in places the sun does not reach. [0, 0, 0] means no extra tint.
terms.RGB color: A color made from red, green, and blue amounts from 0 to 255. [255, 150, 50] is a warm orange.
terms.exposure: How much light reaches the camera. 0 is normal, -1 is darker, 1.25 is brighter.
terms.shadow softness: How blurry shadow edges are. 0 is a crisp edge; 1 is a soft, fuzzy edge.
terms.LightingStyle: The overall look of lighting: `Realistic` or `Soft`.
terms.ClockTime: Time of day as a number of hours. 6.3 is 6:18 AM, because 0.3 of an hour is 18 minutes.
terms.TimeOfDay: The same time of day written as text, like "06:18:00".
terms.GeographicLatitude: How far north or south your world pretends to be, in degrees. It changes where the sun and moon sit in the sky, but not the clock.
terms.diffuse light: Soft light bouncing in from all around. `EnvironmentDiffuseScale` sets how much comes from the sky and surroundings.
terms.specular light: Shiny reflections. `EnvironmentSpecularScale` near 1 makes metal and smooth objects reflect the environment better.

example.title: Simple day-night cycle
example.code:
local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")

local MINUTES_PER_DAY = 4 -- one full game day lasts 4 real minutes
local hoursPerSecond = 24 / (MINUTES_PER_DAY * 60)

Lighting.ClockTime = 6 -- start at sunrise

while true do
	local deltaTime = task.wait(0.1) -- how long we really waited
	-- Move the clock forward; % 24 wraps 24 back around to 0
	Lighting.ClockTime = (Lighting.ClockTime + hoursPerSecond * deltaTime) % 24
end
explain: A full day is set to take 4 real minutes, which is 240 seconds.
`hoursPerSecond` is 24 divided by 240, which is 0.1 game hours each real second.
The loop runs about 10 times a second and adds a bit of time based on how long it really waited.
`% 24` makes the clock wrap from 24 back to 0, so midnight comes around again.
Because this is a server Script, every player sees the same time.

watchOut: Expecting the sun to move on its own. Time only changes if a script changes it.
Changing `ShadowSoftness` while `LightingStyle` is `Soft`. It only works with `Realistic`.
Making `Ambient` too bright. It lights up shadows everywhere, so indoor areas lose their depth.
Thinking `GeographicLatitude` changes the clock. It only moves where the sun and moon appear.
